text:
ara: FYI we're getting a cluster of 5xx errors hitting the hosted inference endpoint since ~11:12 UTC. Customers report intermittent 502s and 504s. Gateway logs show a lot of upstream errors with notes like "control-plane:routing-policy->configdb timeout" and "auth-session lookup failed".

sam: copy. any x-request-id examples? also which region?

ara: sample curl (sanitized):
```bash
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>\" -d '{"prompt":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/generate
```
Response: 
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 11:13:07 GMT
X-Request-ID: rwd-x9z7k-77
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": { "message": "control-plane error: configdb read timeout", "code": 502 } }
```
Region: eu-west-1 for these reports.

ton y: digging traces. routing-policy-service P95 is spiking to 7-12s. traces show multiple retries to configdb with eventual timeout at ~10s. configdb metrics show connection_pool_wait_count jumping and a lot of "waited-for-connection" warnings.

leah: checking configdb host pool. host cpu normal but connection_pool_active == configured_max_conn for multiple minutes starting 11:11. also saw errors: "connection acquire timed out after 10000ms".

devin: is routing policy doing synchronous reads per-request? we recently reverted an async cache patch last month. If requests all hit configdb, a slow configdb will cascade.

sam: immediate mitigation suggestion list:
- flip routing fallback to use local cached policies (flag: routing_local_cache=true)
- toggle configdb fallback to return last-known policy (stale read)
- apply connection-limiter on gateway to backpressure control-plane calls
- restart a subset of configdb read replicas one-by-one if pool leaking connections

ar a: enabling `routing_local_cache=true` for eu-west-1 now (low-risk)

ops-bot: @ara set feature flag `routing_local_cache=true` for eu-west-1 at 11:16:02 UTC

pagerbot: Incident created: INC-20260318-09 52 504 surge due to control-plane configdb timeouts. Paging on-call.

leah: after the cache flag, 5xx rate for eu-west-1 dropped from ~2.3% -> 0.6% within 3 minutes. routing-policy P95 dropped to ~400ms. good hit.

devin: still seeing some auth-related 502s from token validation path. auth-service is falling back to session-store (redis) for some tokens. redis pool shows high used connections and intermittent EHOSTUNREACH from one node.

ton y: recommend rolling the redis-proxy instances in eu-west-1 (one AZ at a time). Also open to temporarily increasing redis client_pool_size but that can exhaust memory on pods.

leah: I'll perform a rolling restart of redis-proxy-a then -b then -c. staging check first.

leah: restarted redis-proxy-a (az-1). monitoring redis errors and auth 502s.

ara: customer note: acme-devops reported 9% errors at 11:15; after changes they report 0.5% at 11:20 and are ok with us continuing investigation. zendesk ticket: https://zendesk.example/ticket/6921. cc: cs.

sam: triage playbook bullets (for oncall doc):
1) confirm symptom: gateway 502/504 rate increased.
2) check control-plane dashboards: routing-policy-service latency, configdb pool usage, auth-service -> session-store errors.
3) run quick commands: 
```bash
# gateway 5xx in last 10m
kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/gateway --since=10m | jq -r '.status' | grep -E '^5' | wc -l
# look for request id in control-plane
kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/control-plane --since=30m | grep rwd-x9z7k-77 -A 40
# configdb pool metrics
kubectl -n redwood get --raw \"/metrics\" | grep configdb_conn_pool_active
```
4) immediate mitigations to test (order): 
- enable `routing_local_cache` for affected region
- rolling restart of redis-proxy/session-proxy (AZ-by-AZ)
- enable degraded routing (fail-open) for VIP customers only
- consider temporary rate-limits on heavy clients to reduce pressure

devin: long-term fixes: add circuit breaker + cached policy TTL ramp-up, add a health probe to configdb to reduce connections before unhealthy, add alert when configdb_conn_pool_active >= 85% for >90s. Also add a small token-introspection cache on auth to reduce session-store pressure.

leah: opened ticket ENG-PLAT-1012: "configdb pool autoscale + routing cache improvements". assigned to platform infra.

ops-bot: metrics snapshot 11:10-11:25 UTC: gateway 5xx: 2.4% -> 0.55% after mitigations. routing-policy P95: 11s -> 0.45s. configdb conn_pool_active: 99% -> 37%.

sam: recommended keeping `routing_local_cache=true` on for 45 minutes and monitor. we'll revert when configdb health returns to normal.

ara: leaving this thread for the postmortem/doc. I'll attach logs and trace links. Trace example: https://tracing.redwood.local/trace/rwd-x9z7k-77

devin: reminder: we should avoid changing max_conn without understanding why it's saturated. likely a blocking query or leaked connections.

leah: agreed. follow-up action: capture open connections at process level and heap profiles for configdb adapter during spike window.

ara: thanks all. I'll tell support bravo to keep customers updated and postmortem the incident once we have root-cause analysis. thread closed for now.
